heart attack = a sudden blockage of blood to part of the heart muscle
stroke = a sudden loss of brain function because blood supply is blocked or a vessel bursts
hypertension = blood pressure that stays too high and damages organs over time
type 2 diabetes = a long-term condition in which the body cannot use insulin properly
tumour = an abnormal lump of cells that may be benign or malignant
cancer treatment = medical care such as surgery, drugs or radiotherapy used against cancer
terminal illness = a disease that cannot be cured and will lead to death
remission = a period when signs of a disease have reduced or disappeared
relapse = the return of an illness after a period of improvement
complication = an extra medical problem that appears because of a disease or treatment
prognosis = a doctor’s judgement of how an illness is likely to develop
diagnosis = the identification of an illness after tests and examination
fracture = a crack or break in a bone
traumatic brain injury = damage to the brain caused by a blow, jolt or penetrating wound
chronic pain = pain that lasts for months and often needs a mix of treatments
occupational disease = an illness caused by conditions at work, such as dust or chemicals
anaphylaxis = a sudden, life-threatening allergic reaction
antibiotic resistance = when bacteria survive drugs that used to kill them
sexually transmitted infection = an infection passed through sexual contact
antibiotic = a medicine that kills bacteria or stops them growing
